correctness.rationale: Direct frame correspondence R⊆R² established by countervaluation. Exact first moment n(n−1)p(1−p²)^(n−2). For every fixed factorial moment, configurations with disjoint endpoints contribute lambda^r by external-vertex independence and negligible internal witnesses. Configurations sharing endpoints are O(n^{2r−1}) and each has probability at most p^r exp(−rnp²+O_r(np³+p²)); they vanish. Factorial moments imply Poisson. Upper regime by the monotone envelope of the first moment; two sparse examples by elementary first moments. The extracted verifier exhausts all n≤4 loop-free digraphs and all valuations.

originality.rationale: The finite-frame validity paper arXiv:2609.10872v1 studies computability of finite-frame validation, not the stated sharp sparse-random distribution. The earlier random-frame literature studies almost-sure/constant-density logic. Targeted current record and publication searches did not identify the exact independently sampled loop-free arc-covering law, its half-log-log shift or limiting parameter. The distinction is one of logical implication and probability regime, not merely terminology. Residual possibility of coverage by an older general rooted-extension theorem is expressly not excluded.
residual_risks: A general theorem on random rooted subgraph extensions or directed triangle covering could subsume the Poisson parameter and centering without naming modal logic.
The highly relevant 2020 Goranko full PDF and the Goranko–Kapron and Karp full papers were not all accessible for whole-document comparison.
Search failure does not establish priority or uniqueness; no independent audit is claimed.

value.rationale: The object is a classical modal density axiom for which finite-frame validity is a concrete structural condition. The sharp sparse transition is not captured by the conventional constant-density almost-sure framework: it locates a nontrivial limiting law with necessary half-log-log correction and explicit constant, and exhibits nonmonotone reentrant validity across natural sparsities. These exact quantitative features are useful for probabilistic finite-model semantics; the contribution is not just rephrasing the known density correspondence.
